research_question: How does the accuracy of one selected open-source LLM differ between original Kazakh and machine-translated Kazakh question-answering datasets?

lexical.description: IDF-weighted sliding-window span selection (group_analysis.baseline_answer, max_len=4, window=6)

xlmr.revision: resolved at run time and recorded

qwen_closed.system: Сұраққа қысқа жауап бер. Түсіндірме қоспа.

runs: one deterministic run per condition (greedy / argmax); uncertainty by 2,000-sample bootstrap, seed 42

hypotheses.H1: Qwen open-book exact-match probability differs between original and translated items (two-sided Fisher exact test, alpha 0.05).
hypotheses.H2: The Qwen original-minus-translated token-F1 gap differs from the lexical-baseline gap (bootstrap 95% CI of the difference-in-differences excludes 0).
hypotheses.H3: With the passage removed, Qwen scores higher on translated (Natural Questions) items than on original (UNT) items (one-sided reading of the bootstrap CI of the closed-book F1 gap: CI entirely below 0).

method_comparisons: Within each group, McNemar exact test on per-item EM for qwen_open vs xlmr, qwen_open vs lexical, xlmr vs lexical; Holm correction over the 6 tests.
additional_analyses: error analysis: 30 randomly sampled qwen_open EM=0 items per group (seed 42), manually coded by two members, Cohen's kappa
subgroup: answer type and passage-length bin
sensitivity: EM vs containment vs F1; excluding auto-flagged items
efficiency: seconds per item per condition
